title: Diamond Foundry Announces First-Ever D200mm Single-Crystal Diamond
zh_title: Diamond Foundry 宣布推出首款 D200mm 单晶金刚石
summary: Diamond Foundry Inc. 今天宣布了材料技术史上的一个重要里程碑：创造出第一颗 D200mm 单晶金刚石，直径为 200 毫米。这一成就标志着人类在半导体相关规模上制造金刚石作为技术材料的能力向前迈出了根本性的一步。在此公告中，Diamond Foundry 首席执行官 Martin Roscheisen 在中国宁波举行的 CarbonSemi 2026 展会上通过视频发表了主题演讲。观看主题演讲：https://youtu.be/ae0XQBDlLMQ 。钻石长期以来被认为是一种非凡的材料
content:
Diamond Foundry Inc. 今天宣布了材料技术史上的一个重要里程碑：创造出第一颗 D200mm 单晶金刚石，直径为 200 毫米。这一成就标志着人类在半导体相关规模上制造金刚石作为技术材料的能力向前迈出了根本性的一步。在此公告中，Diamond Foundry 首席执行官 Martin Roscheisen 在中国宁波举行的 CarbonSemi 2026 展会上通过视频发表了主题演讲。观看主题演讲：https://youtu.be/ae0XQBDlLMQ 。钻石长期以来被认为是一种非凡的技术材料。它将最高的导热率与卓越的机械强度、电绝缘性、光学特性以及极端电子性能的潜力结合在一起。然而，它在先进技术中的使用受到一个基本限制的限制：尺寸。 Diamond Foundry 的 D200mm 突破改变了这一点。生产 D200 毫米尺寸的单晶金刚石需要克服晶体生长、等离子体物理、反应堆工程、材料科学、过程控制和制造方面的基本挑战。结果不是单个金刚石片的组装，也不是多晶金刚石晶片。它是一颗直径为 200 毫米的单晶金刚石。 Diamond Foundry Inc. 首席执行官 Martin Roscheisen 表示：“这是曾经看似几乎不可能实现的里程碑之一。”数百名 DF 工程师、科学家和技术人员为我们实现这一目标做出了贡献。
它是十多年来无数实验、失败、发明、重建机器和见解的积累结果。” Roscheisen 特别认可 Stefan Gsell 和 Martin Fischer，他们在 25 年前就开始了单晶金刚石缩放工作。“Stefan 和 Martin 追求这个目标已经有 25 年了，”Roscheisen 说。 “在技术领域，很少有人能以这种毅力去应对真正艰巨的科学挑战。当普遍观点认为单晶钻石根本无法制造出如此规模时，他们继续前进。如今，这种毅力展现为首颗D200mm单晶钻石。最重要的是，它也使 D300mm 变得可预测。”从宝石尺寸到半导体尺寸 半导体行业是围绕晶圆级制造非凡材料的能力而建立的。硅向更大晶圆的发展改变了电子产品，允许经济且可重复地制造日益复杂的设备。钻石从未有过同等的缩放路径。天然钻石受到地质条件的限制。传统的实验室制造钻石历来被限制在相对较小的晶体尺寸。尽管金刚石的非凡特性与高功率电子、人工智能计算、光学、量子系统和其他先进技术越来越相关，但晶体尺寸仍然是一个基本瓶颈。
D200mm 单晶金刚石里程碑展示了一条超越这一限制的道路。对于 Diamond Foundry 来说，这一成就是更广泛努力的一部分，旨在将单晶金刚石从宝石中测量的稀有材料转变为大规模制造的科技工业半导体基材。当计算系统遇到越来越严格的热约束时，其影响尤为重要。现代人工智能处理器将大量能量集中到硅的微观区域。 Diamond 卓越的散热性能

【原文 English Original】
Diamond Foundry Inc. today announced a major milestone in the history of materials technology: the creation of the first-ever D200mm single-crystal diamond, measuring 200 millimeters in diameter. The achievement marks a fundamental step forward in humanity’s ability to manufacture diamond as a technology material at semiconductor-relevant scale. The announcement accompanies a keynote by Diamond Foundry CEO Martin Roscheisen, delivered by video at CarbonSemi 2026 in Ningbo, China. Watch the keynote: https://youtu.be/ae0XQBDlLMQ . Diamond has long been recognized as an extraordinary material for technology. It combines the highest thermal conductivity with exceptional mechanical strength, electrical insulation, optical properties, and the potential for extreme electronic performance. Yet its use in advanced technology has been constrained by one basic limitation: size. Diamond Foundry’s D200mm breakthrough changes that. Producing single-crystal diamond at D200mm scale required overcoming fundamental challenges in crystal growth, plasma physics, reactor engineering, materials science, process control, and manufacturing. The result is not an assembly of individual diamond pieces and not a polycrystalline diamond wafer. It is a single-crystal diamond at D200mm scale. “This is one of those milestones that once seemed almost impossible,” said Martin Roscheisen, CEO of Diamond Foundry Inc. “Hundreds of DF engineers, scientists, and technicians contributed to us getting here. It is the accumulated result of countless experiments, failures, inventions, rebuilt machines, and insights over more than a decade.” Roscheisen particularly recognized Stefan Gsell and Martin Fischer, whose work on scaling single-crystal diamond began 25 years ago. “Stefan and Martin pursued this goal for 25 years,” Roscheisen said. “There are very few examples in technology of someone sticking to a really hard scientific challenge with that level of perseverance. They kept going when the prevailing view was that single-crystal diamond simply could not be made at this scale. Today, the perseverance shows as the first-ever D200mm single-crystal diamond. And best of all, it makes D300mm predictable as well.” From Gemstone Dimensions to Semiconductor Dimensions The semiconductor industry is built around the ability to manufacture extraordinary materials at wafer scale. Silicon’s progression toward larger wafers transformed electronics by allowing increasingly sophisticated devices to be manufactured economically and repeatably. Diamond has never had an equivalent scaling path. Natural diamond is constrained by geology. Conventional lab-grown diamond has historically been constrained to relatively small crystal dimensions. Even as the extraordinary properties of diamond became increasingly relevant to high-power electronics, AI computing, optics, quantum systems, and other advanced technologies, crystal size remained a fundamental bottleneck. The D200mm single-crystal diamond milestone demonstrates a path beyond that limitation. For Diamond Foundry, the achievement is part of a broader effort to turn single-crystal diamond from a scarce material measured in gemstones into a tech-industrial semiconductor substrate manufactured at scale. The implications are particularly significant as computing systems encounter increasingly severe thermal constraints. Modern AI processors concentrate enormous amounts of power into microscopic regions of silicon. Diamond’s exceptional thermal conductivity can spread that heat at the material level, creating new possibilities for chip architectures, power densities, reliability, and cooling. Twenty-Five Years of Perseverance The D200mm achievement has roots extending well beyond Diamond Foundry itself. For 25 years, Gsell and Fischer pursued the underlying scientific and engineering challenge of growing high-quality single-crystal diamond of scalable size. Their work ultimately became part of a much larger effort involving hundreds of people across Diamond Foundry. The milestone reflects advances spanning plasma generation, growth chemistry, reactor architecture, crystal engineering, thermal management, metrology, automation, and manufacturing. “Technology history is often written around the moment something finally works,” Roscheisen said. “But that moment rests on the people who were willing to spend years — sometimes decades — making it work. This diamond exists because hundreds of people contributed, and because a few people refused to give up on the idea for 25 years.” A New Scale for Diamond Diamond Foundry views D200mm not as an endpoint, but as the beginning of a new manufacturing era for diamond. The company is developing single-crystal diamond for semiconductor and advanced-technology applications where diamond’s combination of thermal, mechanical, electrical, and optical properties can enable performance beyond the limits of conventional materials. The first D200mm crystal is shown as grown and unpolished — directly from the growth process. For a material that nature forms only under extraordinary conditions deep inside the Earth, the significance is simple: Single-crystal diamond has entered the wafer-scale era. title: Lawmakers press Air Force on civilian cuts at China aerospace institute
zh_title: 立法者向空军施压，要求削减中国航天研究院的文职人员
summary: 众议院中国共产党特别委员会的议员们正在敦促空军就其削减中国航天研究院所有文职职位的决定做出答复。在 11 月 4 日致空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 的信中，密歇根州共和党主席约翰·穆勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar) 和加利福尼亚州民主党高级成员罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 要求在 11 月 20 日之前向空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 通报该机构（CASI）的资源配置和人事决策。 CASI 隶属于空军大学，负责管理空军军官学校和士兵学校。 “资源不足的 CASI 使命可能会削弱
content:
众议院中国共产党特别委员会的议员们正在敦促空军就其削减中国航天研究院所有文职职位的决定做出答复。在 11 月 4 日致空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 的信中，密歇根州共和党主席约翰·穆勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar) 和加利福尼亚州民主党高级成员罗·卡纳 (Ro Khanna) 要求在 11 月 20 日之前向空军部长特洛伊·梅克 (Troy Meink) 通报该机构（CASI）的资源配置和人事决策。 CASI 隶属于空军大学，负责管理空军军官学校和士兵学校。议员们写道：“CASI 的任务资源不足可能会削弱军事领导人和文职决策者了解中国航空航天战略和能力的能力，进而阻止北京在军事冲突中使用它们。” “鉴于中国不断努力迅速实现其航空航天部队现代化，同时扩大其在印度-太平洋地区的侵略活动，任何此类专业知识的潜在损失都特别令人担忧。”该特别委员会发布的这封信称，如果没有 CASI 的内部专家，空军和其他机构可能不得不求助于成本高昂的外部承包商。
报告还表示，了解中国人民解放军（PLA）的能力对于遏制冲突至关重要，并且援引 CASI 的章程，对于“提高（美国）在战略竞争中取得成功的能力”至关重要。 CASI主任布伦丹·马尔瓦尼周五告诉《防务新闻》，对该研究所的官方评论现在必须通过管理空军大学的航空教育和训练司令部的公共事务，或来自空军大学本身。 作为一名普通公民，马尔瓦尼表示，他不了解该委员会的计划，但“非常高兴看到国会领导层以完全两党合作的方式行事，表现出强有力的支持”，即使在中期选举季节也是如此。他说：“我很高兴 CASI 的成就和贡献得到了整个党派和政府的高度重视。”马尔瓦尼说，两名 CASI 文职人员已经离开，他们的职位现已取消，无法再填补。空军发言人告诉《防务新闻》，该部门“将直接向委员会做出回应”。该发言人没有回答有关空军 CASI 计划或是否会重新填补空缺职位的问题。目前尚不清楚自 10 月 1 日以来是否有额外的军事人员被分配到该研究所。
议员们在写给梅克的信之前，空军于 9 月份做出了决定，即作为航空教育和训练司令部正在进行的文职重组的一部分，将不再向 CASI 分配文职职位。空军发言人当时告诉《防务新闻》，“CASI 的任务仍在继续，该组织利用指定的军人来实现其目标。”  马尔瓦尼在 9 月份对这一举措进行了不同的描述，称取消该研究所的所有文职职位“实际上是结束了 CASI”。他说，没有任何军事职位受到影响，并指出该研究所有两个军士长职位和一个副职位一年多来一直空缺。当被问及文职人员的削减将如何影响 CASI 的研究时，马尔瓦尼说，“所有研究一直都是由文职人员完成的。”马尔瓦尼在 9 月份表示，此次削减“与 CASI 的使命无关”，但源于以下事实

【原文 English Original】
Lawmakers on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party are pressing the Air Force for answers on its decision to cut all civilian positions at the service’s China Aerospace Studies Institute. In a Nov. 4 letter to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink, Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Ranking Member Ro Khanna, D-Calif., requested a briefing by Nov. 20 on the service’s resourcing and personnel decisions for the institute, known as CASI. CASI falls under Air University, which oversees the Air Force’s officer and enlisted schools. “Under-resourcing CASI’s mission could risk undermining the ability of military leaders and civilian policymakers to understand the PRC’s aerospace strategy and capabilities and, by extension, deter Beijing from using them in a military conflict,” the lawmakers wrote. “Any potential loss of such expertise is particularly worrisome given the PRC’s continued efforts to rapidly modernize its aerospace forces while expanding its aggressive activities in the Indo-Pacific region.” The letter, posted by the select committee , said that without CASI’s in-house experts, the Air Force and other agencies would presumably have to turn to costly outside contractors. It also said understanding the capabilities of China’s People’s Liberation Army, or PLA, is critical for deterring conflict and, citing CASI’s charter , for “improving [the U.S.] ability to be successful in strategic competition.” CASI Director Brendan Mulvaney told Defense News Friday that official comment on the institute now must come through public affairs at Air Education and Training Command, which runs Air University, or from Air University itself.  Speaking as a private citizen, Mulvaney said he did not know about the committee’s plans but was “extremely pleased to see that Congressional Leadership acted in a fully bipartisan manner, showing strong support,” even during the midterm election season. “I am gratified that the accomplishments and contributions made by CASI are highly valued across the aisle and across the government,” he said. Two CASI civilians have already left, Mulvaney said, and their now-defunded positions cannot be refilled. An Air Force spokesperson told Defense News that the service “will respond directly to the committee.” The spokesperson did not answer questions about the Air Force’s plans for CASI or whether vacated positions would be refilled. It is unclear whether any additional military personnel have been assigned to the institute since Oct. 1. The lawmakers’ letter to Meink follows the Air Force’s decision, confirmed in September, that civilian positions would no longer be assigned to CASI as part of an ongoing civilian restructure within Air Education and Training Command.  An Air Force spokesperson told Defense News at the time that “the CASI mission continues, with the organization leveraging assigned military service members to accomplish its objectives.”  Mulvaney described the move differently in September, saying that eliminating all of the institute’s civilian positions was “effectively ending CASI.” No military positions are affected, he said, noting the institute has two master sergeant positions and a deputy position that has remained unfilled for over a year. Asked how the civilian cuts would affect CASI’s research, Mulvaney said, “All of the research has always been done by the civilian personnel.” The cut “had nothing to do with CASI’s mission,” Mulvaney said in September, but stemmed from the fact that the institute does not produce professional military education graduates, Air University’s primary mission. Asked whether another organization would take on CASI’s China aerospace research, Mulvaney said, “Nothing has been identified.” In a Sept. 22 statement , later removed from Air University’s website, Mulvaney said Air University had “decided to close” CASI and that all of its civilian positions would go into unfunded status Oct. 1. Employees would keep working and getting paid in “surplus” status while they looked for new jobs, he said, adding, “I will do my best to make sure they all land someplace that will truly appreciate their talents.” Mulvaney said, “CASI has commitments that it has made and will honor, to the best of our ability, through at least March of 2027.” Once the civilians leave, he said, “CASI will close.” CASI was established in 2017, formally chartered June 15, 2021, and tasked with studying “everything that flies” in China. CASI’s research is unclassified by design, drawing on publicly available Chinese-language sources. It also runs a free three-day PLA Fundamentals course, most recently in August, according to the lawmakers’ letter. The biennial CASI Conference, held in May at National Defense University, drew more than 250 attendees and featured the release of the fifth edition of CASI’s “PLA Aerospace Power” primer. In 2025, nearly 80,000 people visited CASI’s website and downloaded more than 50,000 reports, according to the institute. Mulvaney has said the CASI cuts do not affect the Navy’s China Maritime Studies Institute, the Army War College’s China Landpower Studies Center or the Marine Corps War College’s China Warfighting Initiative.

title: Analysis: China’s quarterly CO2 falls 3% in largest drop since Covid
zh_title: 分析：中国季度二氧化碳排放量下降 3%，创新冠疫情以来最大降幅
summary: 由于霍尔木兹危机继续打击石油需求，煤炭使用量也下降，2026年第三季度中国二氧化碳（CO2）排放量下降了3.1%。这篇客座文章作者：Lauri Myllyvirta，能源与清洁空气研究中心首席分析师 这是自 2022 年新冠疫情封锁以来最大的季度减排量，意味着中国的二氧化碳排放量今年迄今已估计下降了 0.5%。 Carbon Brief 根据官方数据和商业数据进行的新分析显示，2026 年第三季度煤炭使用量同比下降 3%，而石油使用量则同比下降 3%。
content:
由于霍尔木兹危机继续打击石油需求，煤炭使用量也下降，2026年第三季度中国二氧化碳（CO2）排放量下降了3.1%。这篇客座文章作者：Lauri Myllyvirta，能源与清洁空气研究中心首席分析师 这是自 2022 年新冠疫情封锁以来最大的季度减排量，意味着中国的二氧化碳排放量今年迄今已估计下降了 0.5%。 Carbon Brief基于官方数据和商业数据的新分析显示，2026年第三季度煤炭使用量同比下降3%，而石油使用量下降4%。主要驱动因素是电力行业煤炭消费下降、交通运输油消费持续大幅下降以及煤化工增速放缓。中国二氧化碳排放量的大幅下降延续了自2024年3月开始至今已持续两年多的“持平或下降”趋势，如下图所示。本分析的先前迭代中列出的数据源。中国二氧化碳排放的前景取决于不断增长的能源需求、清洁能源增长和政府对GDP放缓的反应之间的平衡。下降驱动因素 2026 年第三季度二氧化碳排放量下降的主要驱动因素包括煤炭发电量下降 3.3%，原因是需求增长放缓以及“浪费”的风能和太阳能发电量下降。
太阳能、风能和核能发电量同比增长110太瓦时（TWh），是总电力需求增长量的两倍多。这相当于德国同期总发电量。尽管中国继续以接近创纪录的速度建设新的煤电产能，但煤电产量和二氧化碳排放量仍出现下降。这意味着燃煤电厂的平均运行时间下降速度甚至超过总发电量下降速度，从而侵蚀了它们的利润。与此同时，运输石油消耗继续大幅下降，2026年第三季度同比下降9%。电动汽车(EV)继续扩大市场份额，9月份创下了乘用车销量的67%和重型卡车销量的50%的纪录。电动汽车的用电量增长了 53%，远远快于道路上电动汽车的数量，这表明现有车队的使用量比燃油汽车的使用量有所增加。其他方面，煤化工行业增长在2026年第三季度继续放缓。该行业一直是排放增长的主要来源，但煤炭价格高企削弱了盈利能力，而较高的产出价格损害了下游需求。最后，随着建筑量收缩加速，水泥和钢铁生产的二氧化碳排放量在第三季度继续下降。
排放展望新冠疫情期间经历了一段时期的异常高增长后，能源消费增长一直在下降，而清洁能源增长强劲。这使得今年清洁发电的增长可能超过能源需求总量的增长，从而维持化石燃料使用的结构性下降。展望未来，这种平衡还依赖于消除新太阳能和风能并网障碍的进展，这会导致一些清洁电力被“浪费”。最近能源需求增长放缓的部分原因（但并非全部原因）是第三季度异常温和的天气。另一个关键因素是GDP增长疲软。然而，由于报告的GDP增长仍在目标范围内

【原文 English Original】
China’s carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions fell by 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, as the Hormuz crisis continued to hit oil demand and coal use also dropped. This guest post is by: Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air This was the largest quarterly reduction since the 2022 Covid lockdowns and means that China’s CO2 emissions have now fallen by an estimated 0.5% in the year to date. The new analysis for Carbon Brief, based on official figures and commercial data, shows that coal use fell by 3% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, while oil was down 4%. The main drivers were a fall in power-sector coal consumption, a continued sharp reduction in transport oil consumption and slowing growth in the coal-to-chemical industry. The sharp decline in China’s CO2 emissions extends a “ flat or falling ” trend that began in March 2024 and has now lasted more than two years, as shown in the figure below. Data sources as listed in previous iterations of this analysis. The outlook for China’s CO2 emissions depends on the balance between rising energy demand, clean-energy growth and the government response to a GDP slowdown . Decline drivers Key drivers of the fall in CO2 in the third quarter of 2026 included a 3.3% drop in coal-power generation, after demand growth slowed and the amount of “ wasted ” wind and solar fell. Power generation from solar, wind and nuclear increased by 110 terawatt hours (TWh) year-on-year, more than twice as much as the growth in total electricity demand. This added clean-power generation equal to Germany’s total power output in the same time period. The fall in coal-power output and CO2 emissions came despite the fact that China continues to build new coal-power capacity at near-record rates . This means that average running hours for coal plants are falling even faster than total generation, eroding their profits. Meanwhile, transport oil consumption continued to fall sharply, down 9% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026. Electric vehicles (EVs) continued to gain market share, hitting a record 67% of passenger car sales and 50% of heavy trucks in September. The amount of electricity used by EVs grew by 53%, much faster than the number of EVs on the road, showing increased usage of the existing fleet in preference to fuelled vehicles. Elsewhere, growth in the coal-to-chemical industry continued to slow down in the third quarter of 2026. The sector has been a key source of emissions growth, but high coal prices have weakened profitability and higher output prices hurt downstream demand . Finally, CO2 emissions from cement and steel production continued to fall in the third quarter, as the contraction in construction volumes accelerated . Outlook for emissions Energy consumption growth has been falling after a period of exceptionally high growth during Covid, while clean-power growth has been robust . This makes it likely that the growth in clean-power generation will exceed total energy demand growth this year, maintaining the structural fall in fossil-fuel use. Looking ahead, this balance also relies on progress in removing barriers to new solar and wind power being added to the grid, which result in some clean electricity being “ wasted ”. The recent slowdown in energy demand growth is partly – but not fully – explained by exceptionally mild weather in the third quarter. Another key factor is weaker GDP growth . Since reported GDP growth remains within target , however, there is reduced pressure for further stimulus policies. The focus of the economic stimulus announced to date is “six networks”, which includes the power grid and the transportation network. content:
资料照片：2019年6月19日，刚刚出狱并投身香港大规模民主抗议活动的活动人士黄之锋在街头接受美国之音(VOA)采访。
美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)星期五(11月6日)发表声明，强烈谴责香港法庭将民主派活动人士黄之锋加判10年监禁。同天，美国、英国等10个国家的政府发表联合声明，呼吁“立即停止对所有受到《国安法》指控的人士的不公正起诉”。
卢比奥国务卿在声明中说：“美国强烈谴责香港法院因黄之锋行使其言论自由而再次将他判刑的决定。他使用和平方式捍卫向香港所有人承诺的权利。”
他还说：“我们呼吁立即释放他以及所有被不公正拘押的人士。”
美国、澳大利亚、加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、荷兰、新西兰和英国政府星期五就黄之锋被判刑以及之前香港支联会领导人以《国安法》被定罪发布联合声明。
这份联合声明说：“黄之锋因《国家安全法》下的又一项指控被判处10年监禁。就在数月前，香港支联会领导人亦因同一法律被定罪。这些事例进一步表明，《国安法》正在被用来针对从事政治表达与政治参与的人士。我们呼吁立即停止对所有受到《国安法》指控的人士的不公正起诉，并敦促中国和香港当局履行其国际承诺，并尊重(1984年)《中英联合声明》所保障的香港民众的权利和自由。”
今年9月，香港法院将长期组织天安门事件烛光守夜活动的香港支联会三名领导人李卓人、邹幸彤及何俊仁判处监禁。
星期四，香港高等法院以“串谋勾结外国势力”的罪名对已在服刑的黄之锋加判10年监禁。
目前黄之锋已经因串谋颠覆罪而正在服56个月的刑期，原本应在明年1月获释。他在颠覆案及勾结案中都承认有罪；这两起案件都是根据北京于2020年在香港施行的《国家安全法》而提起的。
在最新的判决中，香港法院指控黄之锋2020年7月至11月与原香港众志主席罗冠聪等人“串谋请求外国或境外机构等，对中国或香港特区实施制裁、封锁或其他敌对行动。”
现年30岁的黄之锋在14岁时就开始了他的社会活动，并创立了学生团体学民思潮。他后来担任众志党秘书长，并在2014年雨伞运动中发挥了重要作用，并因此两度被判处短期监禁。 2019年，黄之锋加入了香港大规模的民主抗议活动。
资料照片：2019年9月17日，香港活动人士黄之锋与歌手何韵诗在国会及行政当局中国委员会(CECC)在国会山就香港民主运动举行的听证会上作证。
在长达数月的抗议活动中，黄之锋参与了为香港民主和自治寻求国际支持的努力，并会晤了西方官员和议员，包括时任美国众议院议长的南希·佩洛西(Nancy Pelosi)。他还在美国国会及行政当局中国委员会(CECC)在国会山举行的听证会上作证。
黄之锋自2020年11月起一直被拘留，服完新刑期时将年满40岁。
美国众议院中国问题特设委员会主席，来自密歇根州的共和党联邦众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)星期四发表声明，谴责当局对黄之锋的判刑“无耻”。
他在声明中说：“黄之锋是一个敢于对抗威权超级大国的英雄。他之所以对毫无根据的外国勾结罪名认罪，是因为中共系统性地侵蚀了香港的司法独立。”
来自加利福尼亚州的民主党联邦众议员、前议长佩洛西星期四在一份声明中说：“美国和国际社会必须要求立即且无条件地释放黄之锋。”
联合国人权事务高级专员福尔克尔·蒂尔克(Volker Türk)的办公室星期五发表声明，对香港和澳门按照国安法实施严厉惩罚深表关切。
除了黄之锋被香港法庭加判10年监禁外，联合国人权高专办还提到澳门前民主派议员区锦新星期五被判重刑事件。
澳门法院星期五经闭门审判以“颠覆国家政权”罪名判处区锦新12年半监禁。联合国人权高专办提到，审判期间区锦新没有自己选择的律师代表。
蒂尔克再次呼吁“根据国际人权义务，对香港特别行政区、澳门特别行政区及中国其他地区基于国家安全理由所作出的定罪和判刑进行仔细审查”。

content:
台湾海巡署6日表示，侦获4艘中国海警船侵扰金门水域。为应对中国压力，台湾正投入大量资金发展无人载具，本周举行的第一届「台湾海洋科技暨无人载具展」，有具有美台合作背景的STR8及美国MARTAC等防务公司的无人艇参加动态演示，展现无人载具对海洋环境的情报及监视能力。
台湾的政府官员、研究人员及国际防务科技企业本周齐聚台南，参加第一届「台湾海洋科技暨无人载具展」。
与会人员表示，台湾必须加速发展海上无人系统、人工智能以及本土防务科技，以应对日益增长的中国军事威胁及“灰色地带”挑战。
台湾“海洋委员会”主任委员管碧玲表示：“但我们面临着诸多挑战，包括‘灰色地带’骚扰的威胁、自然灾害带来的风险、海上搜救需求，以及保障水下信息安全等——这些都是我们团队所面临的挑战。”
台湾副总统萧美琴说，“面对这些前所未有的挑战，我们的防务思维也必须与时俱进。过去需要依赖大型平台才能执行的任务，如今已可由更灵活、成本相对较低的无人载具来完成。这不仅能让我们宝贵的人力资源得到更有效的运用，还能大幅提升我们整体的防务韧性。”
美国科技防务公司 STR8 Industries展示了该公司的“幽灵尾迹”(Ghostwake)无人艇，菲尔·何(PHIL HO) 是该公司共同创办人。
STR8 INDUSTRIES共同创办人兼执行长菲尔·何说，“看到行政部门和国会都在朝着发展这些能力的方向迈进，这是一个非常积极的信号。归根结底，关键在于‘非对称性’。台湾有2300万人口，因此我们需要考虑‘一对一’的比例——特别是在作战层面，即一名操作员对应一个平台。而借助这类技术，便可实现‘一对多’的模式；这不仅能让你投射出可扩展的作战力量，还能构建起你所需要的非对称优势。”
STR8 INDUSTRIES虽然是一家美国公司，但是总部及研发、制造中心都设在台湾。
STR8 INDUSTRIES共同创办人兼执行长菲尔·何说，“世界上能同时具备上述所有优势的国家并不多——即在高端制造、电子、计算以及造船业方面都有着良好的过往表现。因此，这里是我们进行建设的最佳地点。我们之所以做出这一决定，正是看中了这里能够支持我们业务的技术与制造生态系统。其次，地理位置也至关重要。我们正处于‘第一岛链’的核心地带。从外部视角来看，在印太地区建立这样一个前沿产业基地，对于应对未来可能出现的各种突发状况具有关键意义。”
美国MARTAC公司的Devil Ray T24，以及台湾雷虎科技的海鲨600都参与了动态展演。
台湾国家科技政策智库“科技、民主与社会研究中心”（DSET）国家安全项目副组长方怡然表示，无人系统的发展对台湾的防卫格外重要。
科技、民主与社会研究中心政策分析師方怡然说，“从乌克兰的经验中我们得知，无人水面艇（USV）不仅能执行情报、监视与侦察（ISR）任务，还能进行水雷搜寻及水雷反制（MCM），甚至能执行打击任务；此外，它们在后勤保障方面也能发挥作用。因此，我认为我们当前面临的挑战更为严峻。而我们目前主要依靠的是有人驾驶舰艇和人员，我们需要将这些宝贵的人员和资源留给最关键的任务，同时也为了保障人员的生命安全。这就是为什么无人系统显得如此重要。”
台湾政府强调，中国对台湾周边海域并无管辖权，中方试图通过巡航来宣示管辖权的行为，已违反了国际法。台湾海巡署6日表示，侦获4艘中国海警船侵扰金门水域。为应对中国压力，台湾正投入大量资金发展无人载具，本周举行的第一届「台湾海洋科技暨无人载具展」，有具有美台合作背景的STR8及美国MARTAC等防务公司的无人艇参加动态演示，展现无人载具对海洋环境的情报及监视能力。

content:
资料照片：美国佛罗里达州迈阿密，人们手举美国和古巴国旗走过一家古巴风味的餐馆。(2021年7月18日)
美国国务院星期四(11月5日)公布新一波对古巴制裁的清单，其中包括两家中国电子公司，他们被点名向古巴革命武装部队提供军事装备。
美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)在声明中说，他根据唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统的第14404号行政命令“对在古巴进行压制和威胁美国国家安全与外交政策的责任方实施制裁”。
卢比奥点名了10个目标，包括古巴领导层，原油运输网络，国家进口和技术支持实体，以及为古巴政权军队提供装备的中国供应商。
卢比奥表示，哈瓦那的马克思主义政权依靠其国有企业、合资企业和离岸中介机构的网络来维持其体系。“外国支持者提供军事装备，帮助维持政权的军事力量并支持其残酷镇压，同时支撑其持续威胁、渗透和颠覆美国本土的努力。”他在声明中说。
两家被点名的中国公司分别是中国国企中国电子进出口公司(CEIEC, 简称中电进出口)以及北京华成昊普科技有限公司(Beijing H&C Technologies CO., LTD)。
根据国务院的声明，这两家公司通过古巴的军火采购公司Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A.向古巴军方供货，而该公司在2026年8月已经因协助古巴军方从中国和俄罗斯进口武器而被制裁。
声明指出，中电进出口公司与这家古巴军火采购公司签订合同，计划在2026年向古巴革命武装部队(MINFAR)出口用于军事装备的组件。
2020年11月30日，美国财政部曾根据第13692号行政命令将中电进出口列为制裁对象，原因是其支持委内瑞拉马杜罗政权限制互联网服务、进行数字监控和针对政治对手的网络行动。
北京华成昊普科技有限公司是中国电子科技集团(CETC)国际贸易有限公司(CETCI)旗下位于中国的子公司，出售监控和安全设备。此外，北京华成昊普科技有限公司还在2026年与这家古巴军火采购公司合作，向古巴出口军事装备。
国务院的声明中指出，被列入制裁名单的人员和实体在美国境内或由美国人持有或控制的所有财产及财产权益已被冻结，并且必须向美国外国资产控制办公室(OFAC)报告。此外，由一个或多个被封锁人员单独或合计拥有50%或以上的所有实体也同样被封锁。
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期五在例行记者会上指责美国国务院的制裁行动是“长臂管辖”，并称中国与古巴的合作“光明正大”。
美国国务院声明说，对古巴的制裁是特朗普总统及其盟友为迫使哈瓦那进行政治变革而进行的更大努力的一部分，即使该国仍在应对日益加剧的经济和能源危机，这场危机已经让民众苦不堪言。
特朗普总统9月22日在联合国大会演说时谈及古巴，称古巴是“绝对失败的国家”，并表示“它正以前所未有的方式失败，而且将会垮台”。
众议院拨款委员会国家安全、国务院和相关计划小组委员会主席、共和党议员马里奥·迪亚兹-巴拉特(Mario Diaz-Balart)在当天接受美国之音专访时批评社会主义和共产主义政策带来的“苦难、物资匮乏，以及最终的压迫”。

中新网台北11月6日电 外交​​部周五表示，应巴布亚新几内亚政府再次要求关闭该代表处，台湾将关闭驻巴布亚新几内亚代表处，并撤回所有驻扎人员。
外交部在一份声明中表示，在巴布亚新几内亚最近重申要求台湾人员在规定期限内离境后，外交部在一份声明中表示，这一决定是考虑到台湾的国家尊严、外交自主权和整体利益而做出的。
巴布亚新几内亚7月份单方面宣布将关闭台湾代表处，促使台湾暂停从这个太平洋国家现货市场购买液化天然气（LNG）。
外交部表示，巴布亚新几内亚的行为严重破坏了多年合作建立的互信。它还指责中国利用政治压力和经济影响力干涉其他国家的外交决策并限制台湾的国际空间。
台湾国防部表示，在关闭办事处的同时，台湾将终止在巴布亚新几内亚的所有技术合作和援助计划，包括技术和医疗任务、奖学金和人员培训。
外交部表示，台湾已停止在现货市场上从巴布亚新几内亚购买液化天然气，也不会签署任何新的现货采购合同。
该部门表示，台湾原计划在2026年上半年从巴布亚新几内亚购买约50万吨现货液化天然气。
据外交部称，台湾长期以来一直是巴布亚新几内亚液化天然气出口的主要市场，其采购总量约占这个太平洋国家出口的三分之一。
能源部表示，台湾已评估国内天然气需求，调整采购计划并确保替代供应，以确保在暂停现货采购的情况下保持稳定的能源供应。
外交部重申，台湾是主权独立国家，与中华人民共和国互不隶属。
它还敦促国际社会反对中国利用政治和经济压力影响其他国家的外交决策，限制台湾的国际参与。

Taiwan to close representative office in Papua New Guinea, withdraw staff
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 6 (CNA) Taiwan will close its representative office in Papua New Guinea (PNG) and withdraw all personnel stationed there following renewed demands from the PNG government to shut down the office, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said Friday.
In a statement, MOFA said the decision was made in consideration of Taiwan's national dignity, diplomatic autonomy and overall interests, after PNG recently reiterated its demand that Taiwanese personnel leave the country by a set deadline.
PNG unilaterally announced in July that it would close Taiwan's representative office, prompting Taiwan to suspend spot-market purchases of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the Pacific nation.
MOFA said PNG's actions had seriously undermined the mutual trust built through years of cooperation. It also accused China of using political pressure and economic influence to interfere in other countries' diplomatic decisions and restrict Taiwan's international space.
Along with closing the office, Taiwan will terminate all technical cooperation and assistance programs in PNG, including technical and medical missions, scholarships and personnel training, the ministry said.
Taiwan has already stopped purchasing LNG from PNG on the spot market and will not sign any new spot purchase contracts, MOFA said.
The ministry said Taiwan had originally planned to purchase about 500,000 tonnes of spot LNG from PNG in the first half of 2026.
Taiwan has long been a major market for PNG's LNG exports, with its total purchases accounting for about one-third of the Pacific nation's exports, according to MOFA.
The ministry said Taiwan had assessed its domestic gas demand, adjusted procurement plans and secured alternative supplies to ensure a stable energy supply despite the suspension of spot purchases.
The ministry reiterated that Taiwan is a sovereign, independent country, and that it and the People's Republic of China are not subordinate to each other.
It also urged the international community to oppose China's use of political and economic pressure to influence other countries' diplomatic decisions and restrict Taiwan's international participation.

周五，艺术家胡安博元（右）荣获2026台北艺术奖最高奖。中央通讯社照片2026年11月6日
中新社台北11月6日电 艺术家阮柏远周五荣获2026年台北艺术奖最高奖，其作品探讨了与独裁统治相关的纪念碑在被拆除或拆除后如何获得新的意义。
胡安从 276 份参赛作品中脱颖而出，获得了 55 万新台币（16,767 美元）的奖金，奖金在台北市立美术馆 (TFAM) 展出，该博物馆展出了 10 名决赛入围者的作品。
胡安在获奖感言中表示：“我想从我们这一代人的角度重新思考，我们如何面对似乎已经被充分讨论过的历史，以及我们是否能够找到新的方式来应对它。”
26 岁的胡安毕业于国立台北艺术大学美术系，他于 2023 年开始在立陶宛和 2025 年在捷克共和国驻地期间，在其获奖演讲《寻找 Fronta na maso 下的鼻子》中创作了这两幅作品。
捷克语“Fronta na maso”的意思是“排队买肉”，是对布拉格斯大林纪念碑的一个嘲讽昵称，纪念碑的形状就像人们排队买肉。
仪式结束后，胡安在接受中央社采访时表示，该项目建立在早期利用 3D 打印和数字技术对台湾蒋介石雕像进行探索的基础上。
一件作品将桃园的慈湖纪念雕塑公园与立陶宛南部德鲁斯基宁凯附近的格鲁塔斯公园进行了比较，前者展示了从公共场所拆除的苏联时代纪念碑，后者安置了搬迁的蒋介石雕像。
他说，这两个公园都已成为旅游目的地，改变了游客遇到曾经象征政治权威的物体的方式。
另一件作品通过笑话、口述和网络都市传说探讨了布拉格被拆除的斯大林纪念碑如何幸存下来，让人们通过幽默来看待历史创伤。
该项目还利用生成人工智能、视频和 3D 打印，探索数字技术如何填补历史记忆的空白。
“它从台湾的角度出发，并与全球背景相联系，”胡安说。 “我们都在拆除雕像，都在经历一种转变。我们如何面对这些问题？”
骆丽真馆长表示，自1983年美术馆开馆以来，每年举办一次比赛，为新兴艺术家提供展示作品和探讨当代问题的机会。
她说，今年的决赛入围者讨论的主题包括自然与人造环境之间的关系、记忆与权力以及新材料和技术的使用。
“艺术是我们理解现在、想象未来的重要手段，”罗说。
获得优异奖的艺术家有杨健生、廖昭豪、郭柏彦、苏长庆、蔡昱廷五人，每人价值新台币十二万元。
另外四人获得荣誉奖：陈柏欣、黄冠钧、周韦辰和耿杰生。
展览持续至2027年2月14日。

Artist exploring monuments' afterlives wins Taipei Art Awards top prize
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Artist Juan Po-yuan (right) wins the top prize at the 2026 Taipei Art Awards on Friday. CNA photo Nov. 6, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 6 (CNA) Artist Juan Po-yuan (阮柏遠) won the top prize at the 2026 Taipei Art Awards on Friday for works exploring how monuments associated with authoritarian rule acquire new meanings after being removed or demolished.
Juan was selected from 276 submissions to receive the NT$550,000 (US$16,767) prize at the Taipei Fine Arts Museum (TFAM), where works by the 10 finalists are on display.
"I wanted to rethink, from my generation's perspective, how we confront history that seems to have already been fully discussed, and whether we can find new ways to engage with it," Juan said in his acceptance speech.
Juan, 26, a graduate of Taipei National University of the Arts' Department of Fine Arts, developed the two works in his winning presentation, "Searching for the Nose beneath Fronta na maso," during residencies in Lithuania beginning in 2023 and the Czech Republic in 2025.
The Czech phrase "Fronta na maso," meaning "queue for meat," was a mocking nickname for Prague's Stalin monument, whose figures resembled people lining up to buy meat.
Speaking to CNA after the ceremony, Juan said the project built on earlier explorations of Chiang Kai-shek (蔣介石) statues in Taiwan using 3D printing and digital technology.
One work compares Cihu Memorial Sculpture Park in Taoyuan, which houses relocated Chiang statues, with Grutas Park near Druskininkai in southern Lithuania, which displays Soviet-era monuments removed from public spaces.
Both parks have become tourist destinations, changing how visitors encounter objects once intended to embody political authority, he said.
The other work examines how Prague's demolished Stalin monument survives through jokes, oral accounts and online urban legends, allowing people to approach historical trauma through humor.
Using generative artificial intelligence, video and 3D printing, the project also explores how digital technologies can fill gaps in historical memory.
"It starts from a Taiwanese perspective and connects with a global context," Juan said. "We are all dismantling statues and undergoing a kind of transition. How do we face these questions?"
TFAM Director Loh Li-chen (駱麗真) said the competition has been held annually since the museum opened in 1983, giving emerging artists opportunities to present their work and explore contemporary issues.
This year's finalists addressed themes including the relationship between nature and human-made environments, memory and power, and the use of new materials and technologies, she said.
"Art is an important means for us to understand the present and imagine the future," Loh said.
Five artists received merit awards worth NT$120,000 each: Yong Kian-sam (楊健生), Liao Chao-hao (廖昭豪), Kueh Peh Gan (郭柏彥), Su Chang-ching (蘇長慶) and Tsai Yu-ting (蔡昱廷).
Four others received honorable mentions: Chen Po-hsin (陳柏欣), Huang Kuan-chun (黃冠鈞), Chou Wei-chen (周韋辰) and Keng Chieh-sheng (耿傑生).
The exhibition runs through Feb. 14, 2027.

TABLE TENNIS/Taiwan's Chen wins women's singles table tennis gold at Dakar Youth Olympics
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Table tennis player Chen Min-hsin. Photo courtesy of Team Taiwan at the Youth Olympic Games
Taipei, Nov. 6 (CNA) Taiwanese table tennis player Chen Min-hsin (陳忞昕) won the women's singles title at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games on Thursday (local time), securing Taiwan's first-ever table tennis gold medal at the Youth Olympics.
Chen, 17, defeated Singapore's Loy Ming Ying in the gold medal match in Dakar, Senegal.
After taking a 2-1 lead in games, Chen struggled in the fourth game, which she eventually lost to Loy.
Chen regained control in the fifth game, converting one of three game points to take a 3-2 lead.
The two players were tied at 10-10 in the sixth game before Chen won the next two points to clinch the gold medal.
The victory marked Taiwan's first table tennis gold medal at the Youth Olympics and its fourth medal in the sport since making its debut at the Games in 2010.
Chen said the final was difficult, but she tried to maintain a steady pace and focus on one point at a time.
She also kept reminding herself to push through despite feeling exhausted.
Her coach, Huang Sheng-cheng (黃聖盛), said Loy, the tournament's 10th seed, delivered high-quality serves, but Chen eventually adjusted her tactics and disrupted her opponent's rhythm.
The Youth Olympic Games is an international sporting event organized by the International Olympic Committee for athletes generally aged 14 to 18.

title: 美国中期选举后，140亿美元对台军售案再受关注

content:
在台湾新北市举行的年度“汉光”军事演习期间，台湾军方的一套“爱国者”导弹系统部署在当地一座公园内。(2026年8月6日)
美国民主党预计在中期选举赢得国会参众两院控制权后，一笔仍待美国政府批准的140亿美元对台军售案再度受到关注。台湾国防部长顾立雄星期四(11月5日)表示，将持续与美国国会议员及战争部保持沟通，确保相关军售按计划推进。
曾任兰德公司台湾政策倡议创始主任的国际安全专家郭泓均(Raymond Kuo)对美国之音(VOA)表示，民主党主导的新国会可能加强对行政部门的制约，为推动这笔军售带来新的压力。不过，国会选举结果是否能够转化为军售进展，仍有待观察。
顾立雄当天赴立法院出席追加预算案审查前接受媒体联访时说：“美国国会一向以来就不分党派都会支持台湾增强防卫力量，我们也会持续来跟这些国会议员进行沟通，当然我们也会跟美国战争部保持密切联系，来确保我们的相关军售都能够如计划进行。”
新一届国会将于2027年1月就职。民主党赢得两院多数席位，意味着届时将掌握相关委员会的议程与监督工具，但军售案的推进仍涉及行政部门的批准及国会审查程序。
“与选前相比，我现在对特朗普政府推进这笔军售方案抱有更大的希望，”郭泓均在电邮采访中说。
他认为，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统将对台军售视为与中国谈判的筹码，而民主党取得国会控制权后，可能更积极运用拨款和监督权，要求行政部门落实国会确定的政策优先事项。
“国会的核心权力是财政权：它通过决定资金用于哪些事项，以及投入多少，来确定联邦政府的优先事项，”他说。
郭泓均批评，过去两年，特朗普政府通过扣留资金推动自身政策重点，有时绕过或违背国会意愿。他认为，特朗普在共和党内的影响力，使其较少受到本党议员制约，民主党则不太可能接受同样的做法。
今年5月，参议院两党议员也曾敦促特朗普正式向国会通报这笔军售，强调美国对台湾的支持不应成为与北京谈判的筹码。这些行动显示，推动军售并非只有民主党议员支持。
尽管美国与台湾没有正式外交关系，《台湾关系法》规定，美国向台湾提供维持足够自卫能力所需的防务物资和服务。
特朗普政府去年12月批准了总额约110亿美元的对台军售。另一批约140亿美元的军售方案则仍未获批准。特朗普今年5月与中国领导人习近平会晤后表示暂缓推进，并将其称为“谈判筹码”。
除军售审批外，国会议员更替也将影响台湾在华盛顿的关系网络。
美国台湾观测站(US Taiwan Watch)星期四发表分析指出，本届国会“台湾连线”(Taiwan Caucus)的多名共和党成员将在换届后离任，包括参议员约翰·科宁(John Cornyn)、苏珊·柯林斯(Susan Collins)及乔尼·恩斯特(Joni Ernst)。
众议院方面，离任成员包括麦克·劳勒(Mike Lawler)、布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克(Brian Fitzpatrick)、罗伯·惠特曼(Rob Wittman)、安迪·比格斯(Andy Biggs)和汤姆·蒂凡尼(Tom Tiffany)等。
与此同时，一些具有支持台湾记录的政治人物赢得选举。民主党籍前参议员、参议院台湾连线共同创办人谢罗德·布朗(Sherrod Brown)将重返参院；共和党籍众议员、台湾连线成员安迪·巴尔(Andy Barr)成功转战参院；共和党参议员皮特·里基茨(Pete Ricketts)也赢得连任。
“面对多位台湾连线成员离开国会或退休，台湾仍需要积极接触新一代国会议员，延续并拓展跨党派支持，”美国台湾观测站的文章说。
此次选举也使众议院的台裔议员增加至三人。民主党人、儿科医生及前加州州参议员潘君达(Richard Pan)首次当选联邦众议员，加州的刘云平(Ted Lieu)和纽约州的孟昭文(Grace Meng)则赢得连任。
潘君达的父母来自台湾。他在竞选网站的声明中表示，将致力于强化美台伙伴关系，维护台海和平与稳定。刘云平和孟昭文也是台湾连线的民主党成员。
台湾寻求推进军售之际，中国继续在台湾周边开展军事活动。
台湾国防部星期四通报，截至当天上午6点的24小时内，侦获21架次解放军军机、8艘军舰及8艘公务船在台海周边活动，其中19架次军机越过海峡中线，进入台湾北部、中部、西南及东部空域。台湾军方派遣军机、军舰，并运用岸置导弹系统监控和应处。
美国智库战略与国际研究中心(CSIS)中国实力项目今年2月发布的分析显示，2025年解放军军机进入台湾防空识别区的活动达到3,764架次，比2024年增加22.4%，创下纪录。

title: Beijing Has Little Reason to Welcome America’s Midterm Results
zh_title: 北京没有理由欢迎美国的中期选举结果
summary: 北京没有理由欢迎美国的中期选举结果——《外交官》台北选民20多年来没有选择独立或统一，孟加拉国的唯一不变是政治暴力朝鲜在俄罗斯-乌克兰战争中的表现中国的同伴经济：花钱请人跟我玩印度是在扩大对克什米尔伊斯兰教活动的控制吗？新法律最终会结束亚洲工厂的侵犯人权行为吗？危机中湄公河伊洛瓦底江海豚的谨慎希望 英伟达在哈萨克斯坦巴基斯坦合资企业的承诺和陷阱
content:
北京没有理由欢迎美国的中期选举结果——《外交官》
台北选民没有选择独立或统一
20多年来，孟加拉国的一个不变问题就是政治暴力
朝鲜在俄罗斯-乌克兰战争中的局势
中国的陪伴经济：花钱请人陪我玩

在危机中对湄公河伊洛瓦底江海豚抱有谨慎的希望
英伟达在哈萨克斯坦投资的前景与陷阱
巴基斯坦的人工智能战争
2026 年美国中期选举：对澳大利亚的影响
当选民主党参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科 (James Talarico) 在 2026 年 11 月 3 日选举日向支持者挥手致意。他是 1988 年以来首位当选德克萨斯州参议员的民主党人。
总的来说，北京没有理由庆祝美国中期选举结果。民主党接管国会使中国的战略考量变得更加复杂，威胁到北京从唐纳德·特朗普总统日益交易性的外交政策中获得的一些优势，也许最重要的是，这表明了中国共产党宁愿世界忘记的事情：美国民主仍然有自我纠正的能力。
在解释原因之前，有两个条件是必不可少的。
首先，特朗普背离了长期以来强调联盟、民主价值观、多边机构和捍卫基于规则的国际秩序的美国传统外交政策共识，这不能仅用特朗普的个性来解释。三大结构性发展使美国外交政策的调整不可避免。
美国维持冷战后自由国际秩序的成本越来越高。美国的盟友往往过度依赖美国的安全保障，而华盛顿的国内经济和财政压力却在增加。与此同时，中国非凡的经济、工业和军事崛起从根本上改变了全球力量平衡，使得 20 世纪 90 年代的单极安排越来越不可持续。俄罗斯入侵乌克兰加剧了这两个问题，给华盛顿带来了额外的安全负担，同时暴露了维持国际规则以对抗顽固的修正主义国家的困难。
美国必须做出调整。如果没有特朗普，这种调整可能会更加渐进地进行，理想情况下，随着旧秩序的演变，新的机构和责任会出现。相反，我们正在经历一个国际混乱的危险时期，既定规则的崩溃速度快于替代规则的建立速度。即使特朗普卸任后，美国外交政策也不可能也不应该完全回到特朗普上台前的状态。
第二个资格涉及总统权力。特朗普将继续担任总统两年。美国总统在外交事务上享有相当大的权力，与国内政策制定相比，美国总统通常面临的国会限制更少。民主党国会不能简单地扭转特朗普的对华外交政策，尽管它可以通过立法和预算、加强监督并改变政治激励措施。因此，与立即的战略逆转相比，任何变化都更有可能产生边际后果。
尽管如此，北京有充分的理由看待中期结果

Democratic Senator-elect James Talarico waves to supporters on election day, Nov. 3, 2026. He’s the first Democrat to be elected a senator in Texas since 1988.
On balance, Beijing has little reason to celebrate the United States’ midterm election results. The Democratic takeover of Congress complicates China’s strategic calculations, threatens some of the advantages Beijing has gained from President Donald Trump’s increasingly transactional foreign policy, and, perhaps most importantly, demonstrates something the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) would rather the world forget: U.S. democracy retains the capacity to correct itself.
Before explaining why, two qualifications are essential.
The first is that Trump’s departure from the traditional U.S. foreign policy consensus – which has long emphasized alliances, democratic values, multilateral institutions, and the defense of a rules-based international order – cannot be explained by Trump’s personality alone. Three structural developments have made an adjustment in U.S. foreign policy unavoidable.
The post-Cold War liberal international order has become increasingly expensive for the United States to maintain. U.S. allies have often depended excessively on U.S. security guarantees, while Washington’s domestic economic and fiscal pressures have grown. Meanwhile, China’s extraordinary economic, industrial, and military rise has fundamentally altered the global balance of power, making the unipolar arrangements of the 1990s increasingly unsustainable. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has exacerbated both problems, imposing additional security burdens on Washington while exposing the difficulty of maintaining international rules against determined revisionist powers.
The United States must adjust. Without Trump, that adjustment might have occurred more gradually, ideally allowing new institutions and responsibilities to emerge as the old order evolved. Instead, we are experiencing a dangerous period of international disorder in which established rules are breaking down faster than replacements can be constructed. Even after Trump leaves office, U.S. foreign policy neither can nor should return entirely to its pre-Trump form.
The second qualification concerns presidential power. Trump remains president for another two years. U.S. presidents enjoy considerable authority over foreign affairs, generally facing fewer congressional constraints than in domestic policymaking. A Democratic Congress cannot simply reverse Trump’s diplomacy with China, although it can pass legislation and budgets, increase oversight, and change political incentives. Any change is therefore more likely to be consequential at the margins than an immediate strategic reversal.
Nevertheless, Beijing has good reasons to view the midterm results with concern.
China prefers a transactional U.S. president to one guided by enduring principles and institutional commitments. During his first term, Trump surprised Beijing by launching a trade war that challenged decades of U.S. economic engagement. Chinese leaders initially struggled to understand his methods. Over time, however, Trump’s transactionalism became more pronounced, and Beijing learned to negotiate with him.
Trump has embraced the G2 language, signaling recognition of China as the United States’ principal peer competitor. He has treated Taiwan increasingly as a bargaining instrument, including through delays in arms sales. And he has accepted the language of “constructive strategic stability” advanced by Xi Jinping, opening the possibility of an understanding that prioritizes bilateral accommodation over traditional U.S. commitments.
Beijing recognizes the advantages of this approach. On November 2, the day before the midterms, the South China Morning Post, owned by Chinese conglomerate Alibaba Group, published an article titled “Will ‘strategic stability’ with China go out the window if Trump loses the midterms?” It warned that a Republican loss of the House could test the emerging strategic-stability framework. Yet it also expressed confidence that Trump would continue trying to stabilize relations with Beijing. The concern is revealing. Beijing has learned to work with Trump’s approach and would prefer that it remain largely undisturbed.
Congressional pressure could let values retake a place in U.S. China policy. It could also make Taiwan’s security less vulnerable to presidential bargaining. U.S. policy would remain pragmatic, but democratic values would be harder to exclude from relations with China.
Congress could also encourage the repair of the United States’ relationships with allies in Europe, North America, and the Indo-Pacific. Stronger cooperation with Canada, European democracies, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and other partners would reinforce the democratic world’s collective economic, technological, and military strength. Beijing benefits when Washington quarrels with its allies; it faces greater constraints when they coordinate.
The Iran war presents another consideration. Stronger congressional oversight could increase pressure to end the conflict sooner. China has little reason to welcome an early U.S. disengagement from a war that consumes Washington’s military resources, financial capacity, diplomatic attention, and political energy. A prolonged conflict distracts Washington from the Indo-Pacific and its strategic competition with China.
Advanced semiconductor exports provide an especially revealing example of where Congress could make a difference. Despite substantial bipartisan support for restricting China’s access to sensitive U.S. technology, Trump permitted sales of certain advanced Nvidia chips, including the H200, while retaining restrictions on the most sophisticated products. His administration connected these transactions to financial returns for the United States.
Republican congressional majorities had largely avoided directly confronting Trump’s decisions, despite objections from some China hawks. A Democratic Congress could be considerably more assertive, using hearings, legislation, and budgetary authority to tighten export restrictions. Beijing would certainly prefer fewer such constraints.
Trump’s second administration has generated serious controversies over executive power, the Iran war, sweeping tariffs, allegations of corruption and conflicts of interest, the handling of Epstein-related records, and the politicization of law enforcement. Critics see these developments as threats to constitutional government, the separation of powers, and the rule of law. These concerns deserve scrutiny through democratic institutions, with allegations distinguished from established wrongdoing.
As someone who has devoted much of his life to advancing democracy and human rights, I am particularly sensitive to democratic deterioration. I have heard from compatriots inside China that U.S. democracy has lost considerable appeal. Some friends have even joked that China’s official Xinhua News Agency no longer needs to fabricate negative stories about Washington. Its propagandists need only translate U.S. news reports. That observation contains a painful truth. The United Sates’ democratic weaknesses have provided authoritarian propaganda with powerful material.
Yet the midterm elections demonstrate something Beijing’s propagandists cannot easily explain away. Americans dissatisfied with their government’s direction have used the ballot box to change the balance of political power. The midterm elections created new opportunities for oversight and constitutional checks on the presidency.
On specific policy issues, one may agree or disagree with the voters who produced this outcome. That is not the essential point. The essential point is that U.S. democracy works. It retains the capacity to recognize mistakes, restrain power, and correct its course peacefully.
For Beijing, this is not a welcome result at all. A divided U.S. government can complicate Trump’s transactional diplomacy. A united democratic alliance can constrain China’s geopolitical ambitions. But a self-correcting U.S. democracy challenges something more fundamental: the CCP’s claim that authoritarian governance offers a superior political model.

Amazon’s new basic Kindle proves you don’t need all the bells and whistles
9:18 AM PST · November 7, 2026
In October, Amazon announced its refreshed Kindle lineup, its first significant design overhaul in years. The highlights included a new edge-to-edge design that eliminated traditional raised bezels, thinner and lighter Paperwhite and Colorsoft models with better displays, and page-turning accessories like a Bluetooth remote and a magnetic cover with page-turn buttons.
However, given the impact of the global memory-chip shortage driven by the AI boom, the new Kindles also debuted with pricing that had increased by $40 to $50 across the lineup. That makes it more difficult for the average consumer to consider buying one of the more premium devices.
For that reason, the Kindle I most wanted to get my hands on was the 6-inch entry-level device, which starts at $169.99 for the ad-free version. With the price hikes, this is the Kindle that will remain the most affordable to new e-reader buyers.
The question I weighed was whether or not the basic Kindle is even worth buying at this price when there are arguably better Kindles on the market. The answer, after a couple of weeks of testing, is yes — if you can live without the bells and whistles and prefer a smaller, lighter device.
On the 6-inch Kindle, there’s no warm light to reduce eye strain, no color display, no auto-adjusting brightness, no option to use the page-turn cover, and it’s not waterproof. Obviously, because of its size, the screen is smaller, as is the battery. Battery life is 6 weeks compared with the Paperwhite’s 12 weeks or Colorsoft’s 8 weeks.
Still, even this basic Kindle has seen improvements of its own, mostly from a physical design perspective.
The plastic 2026 Kindle is 11% lighter and 14% thinner than the 2024 model, weighing 140g versus 158g and measuring 6.85mm thick versus 8mm. While this seems like a small change, the 18-gram difference is noticeable and particularly welcome for a device you’re likely to carry in your purse or bag. Plus, it makes it easier to hold for hours on end when you’re really binging your way through a book.
(The aluminum version, meanwhile, is slightly heavier at 162g, or 4 grams more than the 2024 Kindle, though it still benefits from the slimmer design.)
And despite being the “starter” Kindle, the 6-inch basic device still received the new flush-front screen update. This makes it more comfortable to hold in your hand, especially for those long reading sessions. Amazon explained that you don’t have to worry about no longer having a bezel to rest your thumb upon, either, as the new Kindles have been updated to detect a dead zone in the capacitive touch that will readjust to account for the fact that your finger is there.
In practice, that doesn’t mean you can just press your thumb down anywhere on the Kindle’s screen as you hold it — doing so would register this as an attempt to highlight or look up a word. Instead, it means you can rest your thumb or fingers on the outer edge of the Kindle’s screen (the colored border) without triggering an unintentional tap, even though some of your finger will be touching part of the Kindle’s capacitive screen.
In terms of the software, the new basic Kindle is a bit snappier than its 2024 predecessor. This is most noticeable when opening books, which Amazon claims to be 30% faster.
If you’re coming from the 2019 Kindle Basic, the 2026 version is an even bigger upgrade, as you gain USB-C, more storage (from 4GB to 8GB to now 16GB or 32GB), the new flush screen, and the screen resolution jumps from 167 ppi to 300 ppi. It’s faster, thinner, and lighter, too, and the battery lasts weeks longer.
Another perk about the basic Kindle beyond its small size (this thing fits in your jeans’ back pocket!), is that you can now pay a little more for an upgraded version with an aluminum backing instead of plastic and more storage. The new $189.99 aluminum option comes in Seagrass and Alpine Sky hues, and ships with 32GB of storage. Meanwhile, the $169.99 plastic model offers 16GB of storage.
However, even if you go for the less expensive option, you can at least now pick a fun color other than black (aka Graphite), as Amazon has introduced a cheery purple option called Ube. (I almost wish I’d gone for this one, just for the whimsy of it, even though I prefer the feel of the aluminum.)
I should point out that you can use the Kindle Click, the new Bluetooth remote for page turning, with the basic Kindle, but I’m not sure why you’d need to, if not for some accessibility-related reason. The 6-inch Kindle was already the smallest, and now it’s lighter and easier to hold, too. (But perhaps I just don’t get the appeal of the remote? I’ve barely used the remote with my Kobo either!)
The big thing to consider here is whether you want to spend this much on a Kindle that lacks a warm light. While this is something of a personal preference, for some readers, no warm light is a dealbreaker. The warm light shifts the color tone of the Kindle’s display from a cooler bluish-white to a softer amber glow, which is meant to help reduce eye strain and improve reading conditions in low light or at night.
Whether you need this feature depends on where you like to read and how long your sessions tend to be. If you read nightly in bed with little light, you might prefer paying extra for a $199.99 16GB Kindle Paperwhite. (That version only comes in Graphite. The 32GB Paperwhite can come in Seaglass, too, but is $249.99).
If you often read by the pool or on vacation, you also might want to upgrade to a waterproof Kindle.
But if you can live without the extra features and want the best purse- or pocket-sized device, the 6-inch Kindle is still a viable option.

Binance CFO is leaving to ‘pursue a new venture’ after $6.3 billion hack
Binance’s chief financial officer Kaiser Ng is leaving the cryptocurrency exchange.
According to Bloomberg, co-CEO Yi He said in a statement that Ng’s departure will allow him to “pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance,” and that a transition plan has been “implemented over the last half year.”
The announcement comes barely more than a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance users. The company froze withdrawals for several days; after accounts were unfrozen, users withdrew a net $3.6 billion in the first few hours.
Binance and the FBI blamed a North Korean group called TraderTraitor for the hack. The company also said that it would cover all losses, promising, “Binance will bear the financial impact of the stolen funds. These losses will not be passed on to users.”
Ng will be replaced as CFO by Justin Yek.

Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports.
The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo. The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo — supposedly based on U.S. intelligence — also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed.
An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with its customers.
A separate NYT report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company authorized by the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced Nvidia chips. But at the office address listed by New Matrix, reporters only found “a hollow gray shell,” raising concerns that it could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm.
The Nvidia spokesperson said the company sells “the first, best and most of our technology in America.”

乌克兰基辅——欧洲官员本周宣布，数千名欧洲军队将于下周聚集在波兰，参加自愿联盟的首次大型军事演习，这是在与俄罗斯的战争结束后向乌克兰部署多国部队的预演。
特使史蒂夫·威特科夫周一表示，此次演习正值美国、俄罗斯和乌克兰谈判代表定于 11 月 10 日至 11 日在阿布扎比举行会议。这次会议为乌克兰和平谈判动荡的一年画上句号。自二月份美国和以色列开始袭击伊朗后，谈判陷入僵局，直到九月份维特科夫和特使贾里德·库什纳在莫斯科会见了普京，然后才以谈判代表身份前往基辅进行首次访问时，谈判才得以恢复。
英国和法国将于 11 月 9 日至 22 日联合领导 KOALICJA 26.2，汇集来自 11 个国家的 2,800 名士兵，在联军的军事力量乌克兰多国部队 (MNF-U) 的领导下，在波兰、法国和土耳其开展协调活动。美国军队不会参加。
英国国防部声明称，演习将联合空中、陆地和海上力量，“测试如何调动、保护和补给一支部队，以便在战斗结束后帮助重建乌克兰武装部队”。
比利时、爱沙尼亚、法国、德国、立陶宛、荷兰、西班牙、瑞典、土耳其和英国也参与其中。
法国外交部的声明称，此次训练将为部队的最终任务做好准备，其中可能包括保护关键基础设施、训练乌克兰军队、帮助保护天空和清除黑海的地雷，这是乌克兰更广泛的安全保障计划的一部分。
英国国防部长韦斯·斯特里廷在国防部新闻稿中表示：“这次演习表明，英国正在加紧与法国和我们的盟友一起，为乌克兰和平到来的那一天做好准备。这不是一个假设的计划；它是一支真正的力量，准备在战斗停止后帮助乌克兰。”
据报道，多国部队将不承担维持和平或停火监督任务，也不接受北约指挥。只有在停火后并应基辅的要求，它才会进入乌克兰。
前法国驻乌克兰大使盖尔·韦西埃尔 (Gaël Veyssière) 在四月份对《军事时报》表示，停火监测“将是一项与多国部队不同的任务，多国部队的目标本质上是不同的，因为它的目的是支持乌克兰军队的能力得到加强”。
据英国发布的消息称，演习还将测试“部队的指挥和控制安排”，并评估“不同组成部分如何作为一支多国部队进行整合和有效运作”。
英国正在派遣 300 名人员，包括来自被称为“沙漠老鼠”的英国陆军第七轻型机械化旅的士兵，来演练后勤行动。华沙将在战后管理多国部队的调动，但不会派遣其部队

Polish soldiers fire a “Piorun” MANPAD during exercises in Orzysz, Poland, Sept. 17, 2025. (Wojtek Radwanski/AFP via Getty Images)
KYIV, Ukraine — Thousands of European troops will gather in Poland next week for the Coalition of the Willing’s first major military exercise, a rehearsal for deploying a multinational force to Ukraine once the war with Russia comes to an end, European officials announced this week.
The exercise comes as U.S., Russian and Ukrainian negotiators are set to meet in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10 and 11, special envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday. The meeting caps a tumultuous year for Ukraine’s peace talks, which stalled after the U.S. and Israel began striking Iran in February and revived only in September, when Witkoff and fellow envoy Jared Kushner met Putin in Moscow before traveling to Kyiv for their first visit as negotiators.
Britain and France will jointly lead KOALICJA 26.2 from Nov. 9 to 22, bringing together 2,800 troops from 11 nations for coordinated activities in Poland, France and Turkey under the coalition’s military arm, the Multinational Force-Ukraine (MNF-U). American troops will not participate.
The drills will combine air, land and sea forces to “test how to move, protect and supply a force that would help rebuild Ukraine’s Armed Forces once the fighting ends,” according to a British Ministry of Defence statement.
Belgium, Estonia, France, Germany, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Turkey and Britain are also taking part.
The training will prepare troops for the force’s eventual missions, which could include securing critical infrastructure, training Ukraine’s military, helping protect the skies and clearing mines from the Black Sea, as part of a broader package of security guarantees for Ukraine, according to the French ministry’s statement.
“This exercise shows the UK is stepping up, alongside France and our allies, to prepare for the day peace comes to Ukraine. This isn’t a hypothetical plan; it’s a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops,” British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in the ministry’s release.
The MNF-U will reportedly not have a peacekeeping or ceasefire-monitoring mandate or operate under NATO command. It would move into Ukraine only after a ceasefire and at Kyiv’s request.
Ceasefire monitoring “would be a different task from that of the multinational force, whose aim is different in nature because it is meant to support the Ukrainian army in its ability to be beefed up,” former French Ambassador to Ukraine Gaël Veyssière told Military Times in April.
The drills will also test “command-and-control arrangements for the force” and assess “how different components can integrate and operate effectively as one multinational force,” according to the British release.
Britain is sending 300 personnel, including soldiers from the British Army’s 7th Light Mechanised Brigade, known as the “Desert Rats,” to rehearse logistical movements. Warsaw will manage the movement of MNF-U troops after the war but will not send its own soldiers into Ukraine. Nearly 2,000 Polish soldiers will take part in addition to the foreign forces, the Polish ministry said.
France is sending “hundreds” of troops, including a unit equipped with about 50 “contact drones,” the second of its kind after one deployed to Romania, Army Chief of Staff Gen. Jacques de Montgros’s told lawmakers last month.
Turkey will not send troops to Poland, the French ministry said, but will stand up the MNF-U’s maritime element in Istanbul, “testing arrangements for maritime mine clearance to allow commercial shipping to safely return to Ukraine’s ports,” according to the British release.
“This exercise will show that the Multinational Force-Ukraine is a real, capable, readily deployable force that represents a serious commitment from Coalition of the Willing nations to Ukraine’s long-term stability and security,” said the commander of MNF-U, British Lt. Gen. Tom Bateman.
The exercise announcements do not specify the final size of a force that could deploy to Ukraine, but Britain and France said earlier this year that they were prepared to contribute roughly 5,000 troops each.
Even a minimal “tripwire” presence would require 10,000 to 25,000 troops, the Center for Strategic and International Studies assessed last year. Because only a third of any force is frontline-ready at a given time, rotations push that number far higher, Ed Arnold, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute and a former British military officer, told Military Times.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has rejected allowing a foreign troop presence in Ukraine, and he warned in September 2025 that Western forces deployed there would be legitimate targets.
Although the MNF-U is not a peacekeeping force, Polish defense officials said its presence is meant to ease Ukrainian fears of a renewed Russian attack once the war ends.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy pressed allies on Wednesday to move quickly, pointing out that Russian forces continue to batter Ukraine’s power grid and other critical infrastructure as the country braces for its fifth winter of full-scale war.
“Peace has no alternative, and postwar security guarantees must be truly cast-iron,” he said.
Katie Livingstone is the Ukraine correspondent for Defense News and Military Times. Based in Kyiv, she has covered Russia’s full-scale invasion since its first days. She is a former Fulbright fellow whose award-winning work has appeared in outlets across Europe and the U.S.

title: 台湾无党籍立委高金素梅涉接受中国资金违反国安法等罪嫌被起诉
summary: 资料照片：台湾无党籍立法委员高金素梅(左)在日本东京靖国神社前抗议，要求该神社将其祖先灵位移除。(2005年6月14日) 台湾高等检察署星期五(11月6日)起诉无党籍立法委员高金素梅和三名助理，指控高金素梅涉嫌接受中国资金约新台币1.7亿元，在台湾发展组织，违反《国家安全法》和《贪污治罪条例》。检方对高金素梅求刑14年，对疑似已偷渡出境的前办公室主任张俊杰求刑15年。高金素梅否认所有指控，并表示将在审判中提出证据，证明自己清白。 高检署星期一以被告身份传唤高金素梅，并收押两名
content:
资料照片：台湾无党籍立法委员高金素梅(左)在日本东京靖国神社前抗议，要求该神社将其祖先灵位移除。(2005年6月14日)
台湾高等检察署星期五(11月6日)起诉无党籍立法委员高金素梅和三名助理，指控高金素梅涉嫌接受中国资金约新台币1.7亿元，在台湾发展组织，违反《国家安全法》和《贪污治罪条例》。检方对高金素梅求刑14年，对疑似已偷渡出境的前办公室主任张俊杰求刑15年。高金素梅否认所有指控，并表示将在审判中提出证据，证明自己清白。
高检署星期一以被告身份传唤高金素梅，并收押两名助理，随后侦结此案。检方以《国家安全法》中“为大陆地区公务机构发展组织”罪，以及《贪污治罪条例》中“职务上行为收受贿赂”等罪嫌，起诉高金素梅等四人。
高金素梅是台湾泰雅族原住民，2001年以无党籍身份当选原住民选区立法委员至今。
高检署说，高金素梅利用立委职权，就职务上行为，尤其是反军购、两岸、外交与国防等重要议题，依中共授意指示在国会配合发声，影响议事进行，内外勾连，所犯情节极为重大，且侦查中推诿卸责，毫无悔意，建请法官从重处以有期徒刑14年。
高检署也指出，张俊杰以接受中共捐赠原乡部落建设经费为名，透过亲友账户等管道，将新台币1亿7千多万元资金汇入台湾，引进中共资源发展组织。
台湾自由时报报道，检调人员查出，高金素梅明知张俊杰长期提供巨额资金或中共直接捐赠资金为其竞选，她却涉嫌依中共官员及派遣人员授意指示，在立法院内召开反日记者会、对台湾驻日代表处质询删除预算、质询反对军购、透过程序委员会委员身份影响法案审议等，严重影响议事运作；此外，她也针对两岸、外交等议题进行抗议发声，对台湾主权完整、国家安全及社会安定造成重大危害。
台湾中央社的报道说，检调人员查出，高金素梅、其办公室前后任主任张俊杰、陈智葟及助理林怡君等4人自2005年到2016年，将其部落工作队及国会团队统合称“祖灵之邦团队”，以“一套人马，两块招牌”方式运作，由张俊杰、陈智葟同龄团队竞选、问政及联系原乡部落，林怡君则在台湾与中国大陆两边穿梭，接受中共官员指示并传达。
报道说，张俊杰今年6月即遭台北地方检察署以涉嫌诈领助理费起诉，在移到法院审理后以新台币1,000万元交保并佩戴电子手环监控行踪，但他在9月6日破坏手环逃匿，疑似已从基隆偷渡出海。
对于被高检署起诉，高金素梅当天在其脸书帐号上发表声明强调自身清白，否认起诉书中对她的所有指控。
“我没有为中共发展组织，也没有收取任何陆资，起诉书所载犯行均非事实，不能因查缉张俊杰逃亡失利，就草率起诉，转移焦点。”她说，起诉书提到她因靖国神社事件而赴日本及联合国抗议、反对军购等，都是她一贯主张，“并非中共授意，也没有任何对价，更没有一毛钱流入我的口袋。”
她也表示，将在审判中提出相关证据，捍卫自身清白，“决不妥协”。
在高金素梅被检调约谈后，北京当局指责台湾执政的民进党政府是在“操弄司法”，“罗织罪名”，破坏两岸交流合作。

title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang officially called to Congress due to reports of a Chinese spy plot

Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 是一个经常参加大量会议的人，今天他繁忙的日程中又增加了一次会议。美国国会希望就国家安全日益加剧的担忧与黄进行闭门会谈。争取他的时间的国会议员表示，上周的报告促使他可能成为据报道的中国资产间谍活动的目标：Megaspeed 执行官 Alice Huang（与家人无关）。深入了解 TH Premium：AI 和数据中心（图片来源：Microsoft） 数据中心冷却现状 定制 AI ASIC 现状 美国的 AI 芯片规则不断变化 - 世界其他地区正在付出代价 GTC 2026：Ian Buck 新闻问答记录 - 超大规模和 HPC 副总裁就今年搁置 CPX 和运输 LPU 解码发表讲话 对数据中心 CPU 的需求激增，AI 代理负责 该会议由共和党众议院代表 John 组织穆勒纳尔、布莱恩·马斯特和里克·克劳福德分别担任众议院中国委员会、外交事务委员会和情报委员会主席。在众议院关于此事的信函中，议员们表示，上述报道“引发了对中国获取美国技术和信息的重大国家安全担忧”。此前报道的说法是，Alice Huang 是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的中国工厂，正在向北京窃取信息。
《华尔街日报》进一步声称，她因与黄仁勋的现有关系而被中国当局招募。 据《纽约时报》报道，Megaspeed 购买并继续购买价值数十亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片，并自 2024 年以来被美国商务部指控向中国走私价值 20 亿美元的先进芯片。这种情况的背景是，美国长期以来实行出口管制，阻止英伟达和AMD最先进的人工智能加速器芯片进入中国和其他一些国家。这些指控上周首次在《纽约时报》上发表，据报道来自未透露姓名的美国情报官员。众议院表示，与黄仁勋举行简报的目的是讨论“英伟达针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议以及[他]与[...]爱丽丝·黄的互动。”据《纽约时报》报道，首席执行官从未收到过“防御简报”，本质上是对外国间谍活动的潜在目标的警告，让他们熟悉此类活动的迹象。该出版物指出，情报官员常常不愿告知潜在的间谍目标，因为这样做可能会让间谍意识到他们正在接受调查。 《纽约时报》补充说，特朗普总统一年前曾获悉有关 Megaspeed 和 Alice Huang 的情况，但选择不采取行动。
据《华尔街日报》报道，新加坡当局对 Megaspeed 展开了自己的调查，甚至据报道直接询问了 Alice Huang。不过，该国的官方回应告诉《华尔街日报》，新加坡“不执行外国司法管辖区实施的单方面出口管制”，并补充说，在调查 Megaspeed 时，并不是针对 Alice Huang 本人，也不是检查她声称与黄仁勋或中国的关系。 《新加坡人》确实指出，该国对商业欺诈采取“零容忍立场”，并指出该国已因此类不当行为对四家公司和四名个人提出指控，他们可能面临最高 20 年的监禁。与此同时，台湾似乎也在密切关注A

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a man who likely attends numerous meetings, and today one more was added to his busy schedule. The U.S. Congress wants to have a closed-door chat with Huang over mounting concerns about national security. The congressmen bidding for his time say last week's report spurred the move that he may be the target of espionage by a reported Chinese asset: Megaspeed exec Alice Huang (family unrelated). Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible The meeting was set up by Republican House representatives John Moolenaar, Brian Mast, and Rick Crawford, respective Chairs of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence. In the House's letter on the matter, the lawmakers say the aforementioned reports "raise significant national security concerns" about China gaining access to U.S. technology and information. The previously reported claim is that Alice Huang is a Chinese plant in Singaporean data center outfit Megaspeed, siphoning information to Beijing. The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) further claims that she was recruited by Chinese authorities due to her existing relationship with Jensen Huang. Megaspeed reportedly bought and continues to buy billions' worth of Nvidia's chips, according to The New York Times (NYT), and stands accused by the Department of Commerce since 2024 of smuggling $2 billion worth of advanced silicon to China. The backdrop for the situation is that the U.S. has long-standing export controls blocking Nvidia and AMD's most advanced AI accelerator chips from reaching China, among a number of other nations. The allegations were first published last week in the NYT, and are reportedly sourced from unnamed U.S. intelligence officials. The House says the purpose of the briefing with Jensen Huang is to discuss "Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and [his] interactions with [...] Alice Huang." According to the NYT, the CEO never got a "defensive briefing," essentially a warning for potential targets of foreign espionage, to acquaint them with signs of such activities. The publication notes that intelligence officials often hesitate to inform potential targets of espionage, as doing so may make the spy aware they're being investigated. The NYT adds that President Trump was briefed on the situation surrounding Megaspeed and Alice Huang a year ago, but chose not to act on it. According to the WSJ, Singaporean authorities opened their own probe into Megaspeed, and even reportedly questioned Alice Huang directly. However, an official response from the country told the WSJ that it "does not implement unilateral export controls imposed by foreign jurisdictions," adding that while it's investigating Megaspeed, it's not targeting Alice Huang herself or inspecting her claimed ties with Jensen Huang or China. The Singaporean does note that the country has "a zero-tolerance stance" on commercial fraud, pointing out that it's charged four companies and four individuals over such wrongdoings, and that they may face up to 20 years in prison. Meanwhile, Taiwan is also seemingly keeping a close eye on Alice Huang, by inspecting her visits to the nation. The WSJ says that the country's authorities are probing her involvement with China and have her under physical surveillance. As for Nvidia, the company seemingly reposted today the same comments it offered us last week, stating that "meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." The firm adds that "[its] regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security."

title: 馮睎乾：黃之鋒判刑書是怎樣寫成的？
summary: 馮睎乾十三維度 臉書 2026-11-7 黃之鋒判刑書是怎樣寫成的？ 被指「串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全」的黃之鋒，昨日被判囚十年。法官譚耀豪稱黃之鋒、羅冠聰同為主腦，「罪行重大」，判刑須具阻嚇力，並表達「社會對黃之鋒計劃及行為的厭惡」（但社會有多少人厭惡呢？），故以十三年為量刑起點，考慮被告認罪，扣減至監禁十年，其中兩個月零兩日跟「初選案」刑期同時執行。因兩項「国安罪」，三十歲的黃之鋒共須服刑約十四年半，出獄已四十歲了。 黃之鋒究竟犯了什麼大罪，需要重判十年監禁呢
content: 馮睎乾十三維度 臉書  2026-11-7 黃之鋒判刑書是怎樣寫成的？ 被指「串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全」的黃之鋒，昨日被判囚十年。法官譚耀豪稱黃之鋒、羅冠聰同為主腦，「罪行重大」，判刑須具阻嚇力，並表達「社會對黃之鋒計劃及行為的厭惡」（但社會有多少人厭惡呢？），故以十三年為量刑起點，考慮被告認罪，扣減至監禁十年，其中兩個月零兩日跟「初選案」刑期同時執行。因兩項「国安罪」，三十歲的黃之鋒共須服刑約十四年半，出獄已四十歲了。 黃之鋒究竟犯了什麼大罪，需要重判十年監禁呢？宏福苑大火死了168人，政府內那些嚴重瀆職的官吏沒一個坐牢，涉嫌操控「死人授權票」的黃碧嬌仍未被捕，黃之鋒的罪行難道比牠們嚴重？我瀏覽了近萬字的判刑書，想看看黃之鋒幹了什麼傷天害理的壞事，到頭來卻發現唯一的「罪證」，主要集中在判詞第35段，原來就是轉發羅冠聰的臉書貼文。 第35段列出黃之鋒九大「犯罪行為」，出現最頻密的字眼就是「The post was shared by the defendant on his Facebook page on the same day」，即「被告同日將該貼文轉載至他的臉書專頁」——「該貼文」是指羅冠聰的貼文。據判詞說，2020年7月至10月間，羅到英、美呼籲制裁中国及香港，並發起請願要求以色列公司Cellebrite停止向港警供應情報產品，黃則轉發相關貼文。 但光是轉發貼文，有必要判一個年輕人坐牢十年、毁掉他的大好青春嗎？或許連譚耀豪也覺得太欠缺說服力，所以必須把被告寫得更像個滿腹陰謀的「主腦」才行。怎寫呢？最麻煩的是，控方花五年蒐證，根本證明不到有任何外國組織或資金支持被告（見判詞第55段）。跟黎智英一樣，黃之鋒多年來被指「收美國佬錢」，如今經香港警方「fact check」，證實都是子虛烏有。 不知道譚耀豪思索多久，才想通怎樣扣黃之鋒的帽子。但他最後也勉強交到功課。譚在第35段指，當羅冠聰呼籲外國對港實施制裁、封鎖或敵對措施時，「被告的角色就是在香港提供『地下』支援（the defendant’s role was to provide his “underground” support in Hong Kong）」，引起外國關注，增強呼籲效果。譚耀豪為「underground」一字加上引號，似乎是因為他引用了黃之鋒2020年8月在英國《衛報》發表的一篇文章。 我查看該文，黃之鋒是這樣寫的： When certain slogans and songs are forbidden, the city’s protesters use wordplay, songs with Morse code messages, and blank sticky notes to express our grievances. Others even subvert the Chinese Communist party’s own dogma, or the first line of the Chinese anthem “Arise, ye who refuse to be slaves”. Since political organisations are the primary targets of the law, resistance must now go underground, with some, like Nathan Law, fleeing the city to keep speaking out in the international arena. （當某些口號和歌曲被禁，此城的示威者便改以文字遊戲、暗藏摩斯密碼訊息的歌曲，以及空白便利貼來表達不滿。有人甚至反過來挪用中共自身的教條，或国歌的首句「起來，不願做奴隸的人們」，藉此表達抗爭。由於政治組織是這條法律的主要打擊目標，抵抗運動如今只能轉入地下，部分人士則如羅冠聰那樣，逃離香港，繼續在國際舞台上發聲。） 只要不是斷章取義，任何人都明白黃之鋒所謂「go underground」，顯然是呼應前面所述的各種隱微的表達不滿的方式，即港府常常掛在嘴邊的「軟對抗」（不犯法的），而非暗示什麼驚天動地的大陰謀。問題是，判詞列舉的所有「罪行」，其實沒一項符合「underground」定義；也就是說，法庭根本從未證明黃之鋒為羅冠聰提供了任何「地下」支援。 眾所周知，「underground」是秘密的、不見光的，但黃之鋒的「罪行」全是在社交平台公開發布或轉發文章，光明正大，怎可能稱為「underground」呢？但欲加之罪既已無辭，譚耀豪為了交差，已懶理是否自相矛盾，就斷章取義抽出黃之鋒某篇文某個字，霸王硬上弓指黃轉發貼文，就是為羅冠聰提供「地下」支援，胡亂用一個引號便僭建罪名，彷彿兩人真有許多不見得光的勾當。 在正常法治社會，就算像羅冠聰那樣做國際遊說，公開呼籲外國政府向自己的國家施壓，也是合情合理合法的，何況僅僅是轉發貼文？去年9月英國改革黨黨魁法拉奇（Nigel Farage）赴美國國會作證，批評英國《網絡安全法》打壓言論自由，促請美國運用外交及貿易手段向英國施壓。時任英揆施紀賢批評法拉奇唱衰英國，甚至指他遊說美國制裁英國，直斥他不愛國。法拉奇否認要求正式制裁，但承認主張利用經濟及貿易槓桿，迫使英國改變政策。 羅冠聰所做的，和法拉奇差不多，英國政府有出動國安法把法拉奇收監嗎？沒有。如果黃之鋒真的有「罪」，那肯定不是唱衰香港，或支持那些被港官視為「不痛不癢」（曾國衛語）、「一笑置之，嗤之以鼻」（林鄭月娥語）、「完全沒有當是一回事」（鄧炳強語）的制裁，而是他把「国安法」實施後的香港看得太美好了，誤以為自己只要光明磊落，做一些全世界法治社會都合法的事，那就必定不會有問題。 黃之鋒「犯法」時，應該不知道自己正「犯法」，更想不到要重判十年。譚耀豪在第56段寫了一句，是判詞中少數我覺得有理的話：「被告唯一沒意識到的，就是他轉發LKC（羅冠聰）呼籲實施制裁的訊息這一行為，可以被用作證據，證明他與LKC及其他人串謀（The only thing that the defendant did not realize was that his acts of sharing LKC’s messages calling for sanctions could be used as evidence to prove his conspiracy with LKC and others）。」 轉發臉書貼文，居然是導致十年監禁的「串謀證據」，試問除了能夠百分百釘死被告的国安法官外，還有誰意識得到呢？ 相關文章 黃之鋒犯了什麼罪？ https://www.patreon.com/sefirot/posts/16850473 6

图片来源：美国海军 摄影：一等大众传播专家 Jacob I. Allison
2026 年 10 月，中国辽宁舰航母编队穿越巴西兰海峡前往西里伯斯海，这至少是自 2025 年 12 月以来据报道的第二次通过。此次部署还包括穿越吕宋海峡。其意义在于展示通过第一岛链的其他路线。 CSIS 对日本观测结果的分析显示，2025 年辽宁省和山东省在第一岛链以外的停留时间总计为 58 天，高于 2024 年的 32 天。
对于中国来说，这些选择的影响不仅仅是导航。中国不断扩大的海军和空中影响力使其有更多机会向试图中断其海上能源供应的部队施加成本。封锁联盟必须保护自己的业务及其成员的贸易，同时持续对中国施加压力。
就中国而言，马六甲困境指的是其通过马六甲海峡的大部分海运能源进口和贸易受到干扰的风险，以及这种脆弱性给其他国家带来的强制影响力。 《外交家》在之前的分析中已经研究了马六甲海峡的战略重要性，以及制裁和合规压力的破坏性潜力。然而，凭借更广泛的海军和空军存在，中国正在使马六甲困境不再是单向的。任何封锁联盟现在都必须考虑到中国人民解放军（PLA）影响范围的扩大。
解放军的存在使联军规划复杂化的一种具体方式是监视。菲律宾南部的做法说明了这种负担。 USNI新闻报道称，BRP Sarangani跟踪辽宁舰，BRP Diego Silang和BRP Emilio Jacinto也监视该组织。
然而，成功的局部阴影并不能建立持续的覆盖。日本联合参谋部记录了 10 月 14 日的航母飞行行动以及 10 月 15 日编队向南中国海的移动； Bilyonaryo新闻频道获得的菲律宾监测记录描述了10月22日至23日的跟踪情况。这些报告没有考虑到中间的一周。作战情报可能仍处于保密状态，因此这种差距并不会造成失去联系，但公共记录并不支持菲律宾监控不间断的假设。

The Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Carl Vinson (CVN 70) and the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Sterett (DDG 104) transit the Strait of Malacca, July 16, 2025.
Credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Jacob I. Allison
In October 2026, China’s Liaoning carrier group transited the Basilan Strait toward the Celebes Sea, at least its second reported passage since December 2025. The deployment also included a transit through the Luzon Strait. Its significance lies in demonstrating additional routes through the First Island Chain. A CSIS analysis of Japanese observations recorded Liaoning and Shandong beyond the First Island Chain for a combined 58 days in 2025, up from 32 in 2024.
For China, those options have implications beyond mere navigation. China’s expanding naval and air reach gives it more opportunities to impose costs on forces seeking to interrupt its seaborne energy supply. A blockade coalition would have to protect its own operations and its members’ trade while sustaining pressure on China.
In China’s case, the Malacca dilemma refers to its exposure to disruption of the large share of its seaborne energy imports and trade that passes through the Strait of Malacca, as well as to the coercive leverage that this vulnerability gives others. The Diplomat has already examined the strategic importance of the Strait of Malacca in previous analyses, along with and the disruptive potential of sanctions and compliance pressure. With its broader naval and air presence, however, China is making the Malacca dilemma no longer one-directional. Any blockade coalition must now account for the increased reach of the People’s Liberation Army (PLA).
One concrete way that PLA presence complicates coalition planning is surveillance. The southern Philippine approaches illustrate the burden. USNI News reported that BRP Sarangani shadowed Liaoning, while BRP Diego Silang and BRP Emilio Jacinto also monitored the group.
Yet successful local shadowing does not establish continuous coverage. Japan’s Joint Staff documented carrier flight operations on October 14 and the formation’s movement toward the South China Sea on October 15; Philippine monitoring records obtained by Bilyonaryo News Channel described tracking on October 22-23. The intervening week was not accounted for in those reports. Operational intelligence may remain undisclosed, so that gap does not establish lost contact, but the public record doesn’t support an assumption of uninterrupted Philippine surveillance.
USNI described the Philippine military’s force posture in Mindanao as focused on counter-piracy and counterinsurgency missions, while PLA Tracker’s Ben Lewis characterized the Sulu Sea as less closely watched than Luzon. Separately, Chinese ships have used the Sibutu Passage in 2019, well before the Liaoning deployment. Such activity broadens the area in which U.S. partners may need to maintain contact with Chinese forces. If Philippine coverage proves insufficient, additional U.S. or allied surveillance assets would be required, reducing what remains available for other missions.
The surveillance burden created by these southern transits matters even if the coalition does not intend to intercept ships there. A coalition need not patrol every Philippine passage to stop tankers west of Malacca. However, it would have to account for Chinese forces operating elsewhere in the theater and the additional protection required by exposed ships and support facilities. This competition for resources connects the southern transits to blockade sustainability.
Selectivity adds another burden: restricting China-bound cargo while allowing other trade requires more than identifying a vessel’s flag or next port. U.S. maritime sanctions guidance already calls for scrutiny of cargo documentation, counterparties, and ownership. Transshipment through an intermediate hub can complicate the determination of a cargo’s ultimate destination. In a blockade scenario, inspections and disputed records would consume time while Chinese military activity increases force-protection requirements. Shipowners or insurers might withdraw before an interception occurred. Such uncertainty could increase pressure on China, but it could also undermine the credibility of the U.S. promise that allied trade would remain unaffected. China’s regional presence creates leverage by making that promise harder and more expensive to keep.
The United States would face these requirements with a fleet whose sustained availability is already constrained. A 2025 Government Accountability Office review identified shortages of spare parts and qualified maintenance personnel, alongside deferred surface-ship maintenance. An August 2026 report found that maintenance delays and idle time had cost active attack submarines more than 15,000 operational days during fiscal years 2016-2025.
USS Benfold’s July 2026 engineering casualty illustrated the immediate consequences. The destroyer lost power and required towing to Subic Bay before repairs were completed. During a blockade, replacing a disabled ship’s surveillance or escort functions would draw on other assets. The problem is cumulative: more protection against Chinese interference increases demand for ships already needed for rotations, among other additional maintenance and crew-recovery demands. A coalition’s initial strength therefore says little about how much capability it can keep available month after month.
American naval constraints would increase pressure on allies to contribute, but Japan and South Korea have vulnerabilities of their own. U.S. Energy Information Administration data identify both countries as major destinations for crude oil passing through Malacca. Their governments would need assurances that participation would not jeopardize the supplies their economies require. Chinese operations across the wider region could increase the escorts and surveillance needed to protect that shipping route, further draining forces available for coalition enforcement.
The Liaoning’s operation beyond the First Island Chain does not establish an ability to threaten every tanker supplying Northeast Asia, but it illustrates the geographic breadth planners must consider when assessing possible Chinese responses. China could seek to discourage participation in any blockade by increasing the expected cost to coalition members. Allied participation therefore cannot be assumed. Japan’s Reciprocal Access Agreement with the Philippines facilitates defense cooperation, but it does not constitute advance consent to joining a blockade. Contributions to an interdiction operation would also compete with each country’s other defense requirements.
Support from the states bordering the strait is equally consequential. In April, Singaporean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan ruled out participation in attempts to close, interdict, or impose tolls in Singapore’s neighborhood. He described Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia as strategically aligned in keeping the straits open, and said Singapore had conveyed its position on transit passage to both China and United States. The statement directly challenges any assumption that existing security relationships guarantee local support for maritime interdiction. Without cooperation, an enforcing coalition could face longer support routes and more demanding arrangements for access and resupply. Singapore’s position and the Philippines’ surveillance challenge are different constraints: one concerns partner alignment, the other resources and capacity. Together, they show why regional partnerships cannot be treated as ready-made reserve of enforcement capacity.
China nevertheless remains exposed beyond its immediate region. Peacetime transits do not demonstrate the ability to keep ships, aircraft, and replenishment vessels operating under attack.
A 2020 Naval War College study identified PLA logistics, air-defense, and antisubmarine limitations in the Indian Ocean. Rather than establish China’s current capability ceiling, the assessment identifies the functions that distant operations must sustain. Interdiction farther west would stretch Chinese support and protection requirements, rendering the military options demonstrated by operations around the first island chain less feasible. The regional deterrent is therefore conditional and geographically uneven, with its value lying in raising the cost of coercing China rather than eliminating China’s vulnerability to economic pressure.
Only when a coalition seeks to blockade the Malacca Strait or enforce selective interdiction against China do Chinese operations create additional force-protection requirements for coalition forces and exposed shipping. U.S. availability constraints then limit the capacity to meet those requirements, while partners’ exposure makes assurances about permitted trade harder to sustain. These interactions make coalition participation harder to justify. The Malacca dilemma, therefore, increasingly runs both ways. For the United States, the central question is whether a coalition can maintain selective interdiction long enough to meaningfully change China’s calculations while absorbing Chinese counterpressure against its own forces and its most exposed partners.

台北市长竞争对手加大竞选力度；支持高雄盟友 - 焦点台湾
2026年选举/台北市长竞争对手加大竞选力度；支持高雄盟友
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
台北市市长蒋万安（左）和他的民进党挑战者沉彪马（右）。 CNA 合成照片
中新社台北11月7日电 台北市长蒋万安的竞选团队周六呼吁支持者参加11月14日的游行和集会，而民进党挑战者沉伯洋则率领竞选车队穿越台北两个区。
两位台北市长候选人也在高雄分别举行的集会上支持各自政党的候选人，蒋介石亲自出席，而沉在11月28日地方选举前三周则发送了预先录制的视频。
在周六的新闻发布会上，蒋介石的国民党竞选团队公布了一张游行海报，海报上印着他名字中的“安”字，以强调安定和稳定。
游行于周四首次宣布，定于下午 2:30 开始。从南京东路和大安公园两个地点出发，蒋介石的竞选总部。两个团体将在台北市政府外聚集集会。
负责组织蒋介石竞选活动的国民党立委李彦秀告诉中央社，蒋介石将与支持者沿着两条路线之一行走。
体育部长李洋加入沈氏车队，从内湖日出康城扩建部分出发。副总统萧美琴原定在最后一站大湖公园发表讲话。
周六，体育部长李阳（右）加入了彪马沉（左）的车队。中央通讯社照片2026年11月7日
出发前，沉向记者表示，他对李光耀的邀请与他对内湖和南港的政策建议有关，但他没有解释具体原因。
在高雄旗山区，蒋介石与国民党市长候选人柯志恩一起上台，呼吁台北与高雄加强合作。台湾人民党主席黄国昌也发声支持柯。
柯说，自高雄市县合并以来，资源分配不均，她承诺如果当选，将在上任第一个月内设立一个办公室来解决这些不平等问题。

专家：央行在遏制台币波动方面面临问题 - 聚焦台湾
专家：央行在遏制台币波动方面面临问题
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月7日电 市场专家表示，由于外国机构投资者持有大量新台币资产，如果外国投资者继续将资金转移出中国，央行在稳定新台币方面将面临挑战。
国泰世华银行首席经济学家林启超本周早些时候接受中央社采访时表示，随着本地证券交易所规模的扩大，外国机构投资者在本地市场资本中所占的份额已显示出增加的迹象。
政府数据显示，它们在当地市值中的份额从 2024 年底的 43% 上升到 10 月初的近 50%。
此次上涨恰逢台湾证券交易所基准指数从 2025 年 1 月的 23,000 点左右上涨至 10 月 6 日的历史盘中高点 49,968.92 点。
然而，由于担心美国人工智能数据中心的发展可能受到限制，台交所周五下跌1,873.08点，即4.51%，收于39,701.64点，自10月6日以来，该指数已下跌约10,267点，即20.55%。
林说，外国机构投资者在面临股市波动加剧时往往会调整投资组合，由于涉及资金量大，使得央行的工作变得更加困难。
据央行统计，截至10月底，外国投资者持有台湾上市股票、债券和新台币存款1.743万亿美元，相当于台湾外汇储备总额的292%。
林说：“随着他们持有的本地资产不断增加，即使他们只减持1%并将收益转移到海外，央行也将比以往任何时候都更难维持台币的稳定。”
截至10月底，新台币兑美元在2026年已贬值3.2%，并且这种疲软状态一直持续到11月。
周五上午，在股市大幅抛售的影响下，新台币兑美元汇率进一步走弱至新台币33.04元，下午大幅反弹，收于新台币32.768元。
外汇交易商表示，反弹是由于央行干预以及台湾出口商将美元收入兑换成当地货币。
受央行市场干预影响，10月末外汇储备跌破6000亿美元大关，至5964.4亿美元，环比减少43.1亿美元。
央行还表示，10月份境外机构投资者资本净流出约280亿美元。
林说，面对大量资本外流，央行不能仅仅依靠外汇储备作为支撑台币的工具，因为持续的市场干预可能会付出高昂的代价。
他表示，央行需要继续鼓励台湾出口商在暂时不需要外币的情况下将持有的美元兑换成新台币，以帮助缓解本币贬值的压力。
与1-10月期间韩元兑美元升值8.38%相比，台币升值幅度较大。
